outcome: Not resolved. Since 26 Jan 2024 the only progress is partial: structural constraints on planar covers of the reduction graph K₁,₂,₂,₂ (Annor–Nikolayevsky–Payne, arXiv 2412.19560, Dec 2024, revised Jul 2026); an all-surfaces analogue (Briański–Davies–Tan, arXiv 2412.04420, Dec 2024) that does not reach the projective-plane case as far as its abstract shows; Negami’s 2024 J. Math. Soc. Japan paper, which per Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura proves the projective-plane direction for rotation-compatible planar covers, and that group’s second proof of this restricted theorem (arXiv 2606.27703, 26 Jun 2026); and a self-published Zenodo ‘complete, constructive resolution’ by Ren Matsuoka (6 Jun 2026) with no engagement found. Every source I could read still describes the conjecture as open.
problem_asks: Whether every connected graph G that has a finite planar cover (a finite covering graph of G that is itself planar) embeds in the projective plane P². Unpacked: (a) the converse, that every projective-planar graph has a finite planar cover (lift the embedding to the sphere, giving a planar double cover), is classical and is not what is asked, though Negami’s statement is a biconditional and the open half is the ‘only if’ direction; (b) the frozen bullet text does not say ‘connected’, but the literature (and Wikipedia’s Planar cover article) states it for connected graphs, and the hypothesis is needed, since two disjoint copies of K₅ have a planar cover but do not embed in P²; (c) ‘finite’ is part of the cover notion used throughout the literature. Reformulations the literature uses to attack it, recorded here because they bear on what a result must do to settle the bullet: the conjecture is equivalent to K₁,₂,₂,₂ (the octahedron with an apex joined to all six vertices) having no finite planar cover (Archdeacon, Fellows, Hliněný, Negami; reported complete by 1998); equivalently, a connected graph with a planar cover has minimum fold number 1 or 2 (Negami’s ‘1-2-∞’ form, per Wikipedia).

events.what_happened: P. Hliněný, “K₄,₄−e has no finite planar cover”, J. Graph Theory 27 (1998) 51–60. One of the forbidden-graph steps in the reduction of the conjecture to K₁,₂,₂,₂. Known only from its bibliography entry (key K44e) in Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura and a Wikipedia citation; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Shows K₄,₄−e admits no finite planar cover, which removes that graph from the candidate list in the reduction. Restricted to one excluded graph; does not decide the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture in full, including the K₁,₂,₂,₂ cover question.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for graph theory

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (excludes one graph from the candidate list).

events.what_happened: P. Hliněný, a 1998 Charles University (KAM) preprint, later published as “A note on possible extensions of Negami’s conjecture”, J. Graph Theory 32(3) (1999). Proposes a version of the conjecture for higher non-orientable surfaces (for the Klein bottle: a connected graph embeds in the Klein bottle iff it has a Klein-bottle cover) and notes an orientable analogue cannot hold. Read from search snippets and a KAM preprint listing; not opened.
events.revisions: Journal version J. Graph Theory 32(3), 1999 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: An analogue to a different surface: a Klein-bottle version of the question. Does not address projective-plane embeddings of graphs with planar covers, so it is discounted for this bullet.
events.remains: Not applicable: it is a different question.
events.direction: Analogue, not the bullet’s question.

events.what_happened: S. Negami, “The spherical genus and virtually planar graphs”, Discrete Math. 70 (1988) 159–168, cited in Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura as the source of Conjecture 1 (bibliographic key Negami1988PCC; the mapping from key to entry was made by a tool summary and not checked). Most sources date the conjecture to 1988; others give 1986 or 1987. Not opened.
events.delivers: The statement of the conjecture: a connected graph has a finite planar cover iff it embeds in the projective plane. No result toward it.
events.direction: Origin of the conjecture, not a result.

events.what_happened: Y. Suzuki and S. Negami, Yokohama Math. J. 50 (2003) 87–95, on projective-planar double coverings of 3-connected graphs; per a search summary, every projective-planar double covering of a 3-connected graph is planar. Known only from a repository listing and a search summary; the paper was not opened and the first name of Suzuki is not verified.
events.delivers: Two-fold case only: for 3-connected graphs, projective-planar double covers are planar. Says nothing about covers of fold 3 or more.
events.remains: All covers of fold 3 or more, and the general conjecture.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture, two-fold covers only.

events.what_happened: S. Negami, “Tower construction of planar coverings of graphs” (Japanese title グラフの平面的被覆の搭載成法), Information and Communication Studies (Bunkyo University) No. 25 (2000), pp. 25–29; repository record added 2011. Shows a connected graph is projective-planar iff it has a chain of double coverings Gₙ→…→G₀ with Gₙ planar (a planar tower), and iff it has a projective-planar double covering. Presented as evidence for the conjecture. Repository record read; PDF not read.
events.delivers: A tower characterisation of projective-planarity by double covers. Covers of fold 2 and tower chains only; not the conjecture for arbitrary planar covers.
events.remains: Covers of any fold other than the tower case; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: S. Negami, “Projective-planar double coverings of graphs”, European J. Combin. (2005), per search snippets (volume not verified). Shows a connected graph is projective-planar iff it has a planar double covering, and that any projective-planar double covering of a 2-connected nonplanar graph is planar. Known from a search summary and a slide deck; not opened.
events.delivers: Settles the two-fold case: a connected graph is projective-planar iff it has a planar double cover. Covers of fold 3 or more are not addressed.
events.remains: Covers of fold 3 or more; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Settles the two-fold case of the conjecture, leaves higher folds open.

events.what_happened: Y. Rieck and Y. Yamashita, “On Negami’s planar cover conjecture”, arXiv math/0612342 (v1 13 Dec 2006, 20 pp., 13 figures; no later versions). Defines two properties, V and E, of a cover together with an embedding of its planar cover in the sphere; shows that a cover with both properties forces G to embed in P². Regular covers always satisfy both; gives an irregular example. Asks whether the conjecture holds for weak covers (Question 1.2). Abstract page read; journal publication not located.
events.delivers: Restricted: for covers satisfying Properties V and E (including all regular covers), G embeds in P². Does not settle the general statement.
events.remains: Covers failing Properties V and E; weak covers (their Question 1.2).
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (restricted class of covers).

events.what_happened: P. Hliněný and R. Thomas, “On possible counterexamples to Negami’s planar cover conjecture”, J. Graph Theory 46(3) (2004) 183–206 (manuscript cited as 1999). Shows that, up to obvious constructions, there are at most 16 possible counterexamples, and gives a finite list of candidate excluded-minor sets for the planar-cover property. Read from a repository record and search snippets; the article was not opened.
events.revisions: Journal version 2004; earlier manuscript cited as 1999.
events.delivers: Narrows any counterexample to at most 16 candidates up to obvious constructions. Does not decide the conjecture, and does not rule any candidate in or out.
events.remains: Whether any of the at most 16 candidates is a counterexample; the conjecture itself.
events.direction: Narrowing toward the conjecture; cuts neither way.

events.what_happened: Y. Rieck and Y. Yamashita, “Finite planar emulators for K₄,₅−4K₂ and K₁,₂,₂,₂ and Fellows’ conjecture”, arXiv 0812.3700 (v1 19 Dec 2008; v2 6 Jan 2009; v3 26 Jun 2009, final version); published Eur. J. Combin. 31 (2010) 903. Constructs a finite planar emulator for K₁,₂,₂,₂ and for K₄,₅−4K₂ (a counterexample to Fellows’ 1988 conjecture), and states that Negami’s conjecture holds iff K₁,₂,₂,₂ has no finite planar cover, which the paper leaves unresolved. Abstract page read.
events.revisions: v2 6 Jan 2009; v3 26 Jun 2009 (final, to appear in Eur. J. Combin.).
events.delivers: Existence of a finite planar emulator for K₁,₂,₂,₂ (a weaker notion than a cover). Explicitly does not decide whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has a finite planar cover.
events.remains: Whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has a finite planar cover, which is equivalent to the conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the final version (journal reference on arXiv page)

events.direction: Neutral toward the conjecture: an emulator for K₁,₂,₂,₂ does not decide whether a cover exists.
events.object: Finite planar emulator for K₁,₂,₂,₂ (a weaker structure than a planar cover); not a cover, and not a decision on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: P. Hliněný, “20 Years of Negami’s Planar Cover Conjecture”, Graphs and Combinatorics 26(4) (2010) 525–536 (DOI 10.1007/s00373-010-0934-9). A survey of partial results, stating the conjecture is still open after more than 20 years of work. The same abstract was given as a talk at the 20th Workshop on Topological Graph Theory, Yokohama, in 2008. Read from search snippets and publication listings; the PDF was returned as unreadable binary.
events.delivers: No new result. A status statement: open in 2008.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; author is a graph theorist working on the problem

events.direction: Status: open.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2311.01672 v1, “Counterexamples to Negami’s Conjecture have ply at least 14”, by Dickson Y. B. Annor, Yuri Nikolayevsky and Michael S. Payne. Proves that K₁,₂,₂,₂ (written K₂,₂,₂,₁ in the v1 abstract) has no planar cover of ply less than 14, so any counterexample has ply at least 14 and at least 98 vertices. v1 abstract read; v1 full text not read. Subject math.CO, MSC 05C10 and 57M15.
events.revisions: v2 10 Sep 2024 (current), retitled “K₁,₂,₂,₂ has no n-fold planar cover graph for n<14”. v2 restates the result by fold number: Theorem 1, no 4-, 6-, 8-, 10- or 12-fold cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂ is planar; a corollary, using a parity result for planar covers of nonplanar graphs (attributed to Archdeacon and Richter), gives fold number <14 for connected graphs. A 2025 listing gives Graphs and Combinatorics 41(6), article 126 (DOI 10.1007/s00373-025-02983-w); the listing title was seen in search results, the page itself returned HTTP 403.
events.delivers: A restricted case of the conjecture: for a connected graph with a planar cover of ply (fold number) below 14, the conjecture holds, because the conjecture is equivalent to K₁,₂,₂,₂ having no finite planar cover. Covers of K₁,₂,₂,₂ of ply 14 or more are not addressed.
events.remains: Whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has a finite planar cover of any ply 14 or more, which is equivalent to the full conjecture. No upper bound on the ply of a smallest such cover is known (per Briański–Davies–Tan).

checked_by.who: Graphs and Combinatorics (Springer), journal of record
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication in 2025 (listing seen in search results; article not opened)

events.time_since_posted: 35 months since v1; no separate public check found beyond the journal
events.directly_checkable: The result is non-existence of planar covers of a 7-vertex graph (K₁,₂,₂,₂) with fold number below 14. The paper argues by structural lemmas (a cover of minimal fold with most triangular faces); no computer search is mentioned in the v2 text read.
events.doubts: Scope wording changed between versions. v1 states the result for ply and for counterexamples (ply at least 14, 98 vertices). v2 states it by fold number, proves even folds 4 to 12, and reaches fold below 14 via a parity result. Whether v1’s argument covers odd ply without that step was not checked, because the v1 full text was not read. This is a scope check for the judging pass, not an error signal.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in restricted form: rules out putative counterexamples of ply below 14. Does not decide the conjecture.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2412.19560, “Three Theorems on Negami’s Planar Cover Conjecture”, by Annor, Nikolayevsky and Payne. Theorem 1: if K is 4-connected, a minimal planar cover of K is 4-connected. Theorems 2 and 3 restrict any planar cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂: Theorem 2 forbids a planar cover in which the closed neighbourhood of each vertex over the apex induces the wheel W₇; Theorem 3 says a certain subgraph H cannot have all its internal non-triangular faces of length 9. Consequence: a minimal planar cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂, if one exists, is 4-connected. Read from the arXiv abstract page and HTML v2; quotes limited, so the wording of Theorems 2 and 3 is partial.
events.revisions: v2 17 Jul 2026 (arXiv stamp 2412.19560v2 [math.CO] 17 Jul 2026). The text read has no version notes, so the changes between v1 and v2 are not identified. No journal publication found.
events.delivers: Structural constraints on any planar cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂ (Theorems 2 and 3), and a general 4-connectivity statement for minimal planar covers of 4-connected graphs (Theorem 1). Gives no fold or ply bound beyond the 2023 paper, and does not decide whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has a planar cover.
events.remains: Whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has any finite planar cover, which is equivalent to the full conjecture.

checked_by.qualification: Referee for a journal version (journal not identified)
checked_by.what_they_did: Suggested an idea that substantially simplified the proof, per footnote in the HTML v2

events.time_since_posted: 22 months since v1; no public check beyond the referee footnote found
events.directly_checkable: The restrictions concern covers of a 7-vertex graph and are checkable by hand in principle; the proofs are by hand, and no computation is mentioned.
events.direction: Constraints on a putative counterexample: supports the conjecture in restricted form. Not a resolution.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2412.04420, “On high genus extensions of Negami’s conjecture”, by Marcin Briański, James Davies and Jane Tan (v1 only; 14 pp., 1 figure). Proposes that for every compact surface Σ, a connected graph has a finite cover embeddable in Σ iff it embeds in some surface covered by Σ. Shows that such graphs have bounded Euler genus (for Euler genus at least a constant c, the ply is at most a decreasing function p_Σ(g)), gives decidability for surfaces of large Euler genus, and a countable-graph version for orientable surfaces. Abstract page read only. Cites the Annor–Nikolayevsky–Payne ply-13 result as recent.
events.delivers: An analogue on every surface, with theorems for graphs of large Euler genus. As far as the abstract states, these theorems do not reach the projective plane (Euler genus 1); the constant c is not read. Does not settle Negami’s conjecture as stated.
events.remains: The projective-plane statement of the bullet, which the abstract’s theorems do not address.
events.time_since_posted: 22 months; no third-party check of this paper found
events.direction: Analogue for all surfaces; not the bullet’s question. Discounted for the bullet.

events.what_happened: S. Negami, “Another approach to Planar Cover Conjecture focusing on rotation systems”, J. Math. Soc. Japan 76(3) (2024), pp. 975–996 (issue dated July 2024 on the Mathematical Society of Japan index). Per Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura, its Theorem 2 (attributed to Negami) says that a connected graph has a finite rotation-compatible planar cover iff it embeds in the projective plane. Rotation compatibility is two assumptions on a cover with an orientable rotation system: fibre rotations agree up to inversion, and each edge’s lifts are all synchronous or all anti-synchronous. The proof uses algebraic and topological methods, including regular and branched covers of surfaces (per the same source). The paper itself was not reached.
events.delivers: For connected graphs: the ‘only if’ direction holds when the planar cover is rotation compatible. This is a restriction on the class of covers, not the general statement. An earlier public version may exist; none was found, so the date is the journal year.
events.remains: Planar covers that are not rotation compatible. Whether every connected graph with a finite planar cover also has a rotation-compatible one is not established by anything I read. A search-result summary, not a source, suggests the paper frames this as the step that would settle the conjecture; I could not confirm that from the paper’s text.

checked_by.who: Shohei Koizumi, Yusuke Suzuki, Kensuke Tamura (affiliation Niigata University, per search snippet)
checked_by.qualification: Combinatorialists who re-proved and cited the theorem
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a second, mainly combinatorial proof of this theorem (arXiv 2606.27703, Jun 2026)

checked_by.who: Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan

events.doubts: I did not read the paper first-hand. Its claimed reach comes from the Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura introduction, read through a tool summary, so the restriction and its attribution are secondhand.
events.direction: Positive for a restricted class: proves the ‘only if’ direction for rotation-compatible planar covers, and leaves other covers open.

events.what_happened: arXiv 2606.27703, “Another proof of the result on rotation compatible planar covers”, by Shohei Koizumi, Yusuke Suzuki and Kensuke Tamura. Gives a second proof, mainly combinatorial (structural analysis relative to a spanning tree of the base graph), of Negami’s theorem that a connected graph has a finite rotation-compatible planar cover iff it embeds in the projective plane; the earlier proof used algebraic and topological methods. States Conjecture 1 (Negami’s Planar Cover Conjecture) as the general statement. Read from the arXiv abstract page and HTML v1 (introduction, theorem numbering, bibliography, acknowledgements).
events.delivers: No new case. Re-proves the rotation-compatible case of the conjecture (Negami’s Theorem 2), restricted to covers satisfying the two rotation-compatibility assumptions.
events.remains: The general conjecture: planar covers that are not rotation compatible.
events.time_since_posted: 3.5 months; no third-party reading found. The paper is itself a re-proof of Negami’s theorem.
events.direction: Same as the Negami 2024 event: positive for the restricted class.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 20569230 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20569230), “A Proof of Negami’s Planar Cover Conjecture via Dynamic Wave-Point Geometry and Pinned Laplacian Singularity Systems”. Sole creator Ren Matsuoka (no affiliation given), CC BY 4.0, resource type “Preprint”. The description says “This monograph presents a complete, constructive resolution of Negami’s Planar Cover Conjecture (1986)”. Per the description (abstract page and Zenodo API), the method models graphs as dynamic topological spaces, uses an “outward-directed tension flow” to untangle crossings, a “Pinned Discrete Laplacian System” to invert layer-switching matrices, and “wave-action conservation laws” to bound the covering index. Sole keyword: “wave point geometry”. Views 38, downloads 20 at the time read. The PDF body was not readable with my tools.
events.revisions: Zenodo metadata: revision 4; created 2026-06-06 09:19:37 UTC, last modified 09:20:10 UTC (33 seconds later). One version only.
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture: every connected graph with a finite planar cover embeds in P². The description gives no lemma, theorem list, or explicit cover, so I cannot say what the proof contains.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim held. Not verified.
events.doubts: (1) Sole author, no affiliation, self-published on Zenodo, which does not referee. (2) The description’s vocabulary (‘Dynamic Wave-Point Geometry’, ‘outward-directed tension flow’, ‘wave-action conservation laws’) does not match the topological graph theory in which the conjecture is stated, and I could not map any step onto cover-theoretic definitions. (3) The description gives the conjecture’s date as 1986; the literature gives 1988. (4) The same creator has a series of Zenodo records titled ‘wave point geometry’ (v5 27 May 2026 through v11 19 Jun 2026, per search results). One of them (record 20608320, 9 Jun 2026) was read: it describes a general framework of geometry from phase on discrete networks and does not mention planar covers. (5) The description, as read, cites none of the literature on planar covers. (6) No review, citation, comment, or refutation was found in any search.
events.direction: Claims to prove the conjecture in the direction asked (planar cover implies projective-planar). Unverified.

disputes.summary: Year of the conjecture: 1988 in most sources (Negami 1988 cited by Hliněný’s survey, the Annor et al. papers, Wikipedia and Koizumi et al.); 1986 in the Matsuoka Zenodo description; 1986 and 1987 also appear in search summaries. Not a priority dispute, but the record should not fix the year without the later pass’s choice.

Name of the graph and form of the result in the 2023 preprint: v1 writes K₂,₂,₂,₁ and ‘ply’; v2 writes K₁,₂,₂,₂ and ‘fold number’ (the same graph, since the parts are 1,2,2,2). Both are the reduction graph, so this is naming, not a second result.

summary: I ran 44 web searches (43 standard, one extended) and opened 15 sources: arXiv abstracts and HTML versions, the Zenodo record and its API, Wikipedia’s Planar cover article, and the Bunkyo repository record. The rest were read as search snippets and are marked unopened. No resolution, no counterexample, no withdrawal, no Lean or Coq formalisation, and no AI-credited result for this conjecture turned up. Every source I could read still describes the conjecture as open, and Wikipedia’s Planar cover article (last edited 25 Jul 2025) says it remains unsolved. The reduction is what matters for judging any result: the conjecture is equivalent to K₁,₂,₂,₂ having no finite planar cover, and the reduction was complete by 1998, so every in-window result is partial. In-window events: (i) Annor–Nikolayevsky–Payne, arXiv 2412.19560 (27 Dec 2024; v2 17 Jul 2026), which gives structural constraints on planar covers of K₁,₂,₂,₂ and a 4-connectivity result for minimal covers of 4-connected graphs; (ii) Briański–Davies–Tan, arXiv 2412.04420 (5 Dec 2024), an all-surfaces analogue whose theorems, as far as the abstract shows, concern large Euler genus and do not reach the projective plane; (iii) Negami’s 2024 J. Math. Soc. Japan paper, which per Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura proves the ‘only if’ direction for rotation-compatible planar covers, and Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura’s second, combinatorial proof of that restricted theorem (arXiv 2606.27703, 26 Jun 2026); (iv) a Zenodo record by Ren Matsuoka (6 Jun 2026) claiming a complete, constructive proof, with no engagement found. The 2023 preprint by the same authors (v1 3 Nov 2023, which predates the frozen revision; v2 10 Sep 2024, in the window) is the strongest partial result: it shows K₁,₂,₂,₂ has no finite planar cover of ply or fold number below 14, so any counterexample needs ply at least 14 and at least 98 vertices (v1); it is listed as published in Graphs and Combinatorics 41(6), 2025, from a listing I could not open. Two readings are close. First, the Negami/Koizumi result: read literally it settles the conjecture only for rotation-compatible covers; it settles the whole conjecture only if every planar cover of a connected graph can be made rotation compatible, which I could not confirm. Second, the Matsuoka record: the abstract makes the claim explicitly, but I could not tie any step to cover theory, the PDF was not readable, and I have recorded it as an unverified claim, not as a resolution. For AI involvement, I ran several AI-specific searches (AI-lab names, AI-generated proof, Zenodo and LLM terms, and AI trackers); none linked an AI system to this conjecture, and every record I read has no AI statement in its text. The 2026 AI graph-theory claims I found (OpenAI’s cycle double cover proof, July 2026, and others) concern different problems and are not recorded as events. The 1986/1987/1988 date conflict is recorded as a dispute, not researched further.
competing_reading: For the Matsuoka record: it is a public, explicit claim to a complete, constructive resolution, and four months without uptake is normal for a sole-author self-published preprint, so the absence of engagement is not evidence the proof is wrong. Against this, the abstract names no lemma, no explicit cover, and no earlier literature, and its vocabulary does not match the topological graph theory in which the conjecture is stated. For the Negami/Koizumi result: one can read it as a substantive reduction, since a rotation-compatibility reduction would settle the conjecture if all planar covers can be made rotation compatible, and the search summary says the paper frames it that way. The other reading is that it proves a restricted class and nothing more, which is what Theorem 2, as stated, literally says. For the 2023 preprint: one can read the result as a bound on counterexamples, which is how its authors present it, or as a complete case analysis for a single graph, which the reduction makes equivalent to the whole conjecture only if the case analysis is extended to all fold numbers.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The full text of Negami 2024 (J. Math. Soc. Japan 76(3), pp. 975–996) and Section 1 of Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura, to decide whether rotation compatibility is automatic for planar covers of connected graphs. (b) A refereed decision, expert write-up, or Lean formalisation of the Matsuoka record’s argument; its PDF body was not readable with my tools. (c) The published Graphs and Combinatorics 41(6) (2025) article for the Annor et al. 2023 result, to check that its statement matches the v2 fold-number wording and whether v1’s argument covers odd ply. (d) Any proof or counterexample for K₁,₂,₂,₂ with fold number 14 or more, since every resolution of the conjecture passes through that one graph.

event.what_happened: arXiv 2412.19560, “Three Theorems on Negami’s Planar Cover Conjecture”, by Annor, Nikolayevsky and Payne. Theorem 1: if K is 4-connected, a minimal planar cover of K is 4-connected. Theorems 2 and 3 restrict any planar cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂: Theorem 2 forbids a planar cover in which the closed neighbourhood of each vertex over the apex induces the wheel W₇; Theorem 3 says a certain subgraph H cannot have all its internal non-triangular faces of length 9. Consequence: a minimal planar cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂, if one exists, is 4-connected. Read from the arXiv abstract page and HTML v2; quotes limited, so the wording of Theorems 2 and 3 is partial.
event.revisions: v2 17 Jul 2026 (arXiv stamp 2412.19560v2 [math.CO] 17 Jul 2026). The text read has no version notes, so the changes between v1 and v2 are not identified. No journal publication found.
event.delivers: Structural constraints on any planar cover of K₁,₂,₂,₂ (Theorems 2 and 3), and a general 4-connectivity statement for minimal planar covers of 4-connected graphs (Theorem 1). Gives no fold or ply bound beyond the 2023 paper, and does not decide whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has a planar cover.
event.remains: Whether K₁,₂,₂,₂ has any finite planar cover, which is equivalent to the full conjecture.

events.credibility_reason: Several F10 signals together: sole unaffiliated author self-publishing on a non-refereeing venue a full resolution of a decades-old landmark problem; vocabulary ('wave-point geometry', 'tension flow', 'wave-action conservation laws') foreign to topological graph theory with no mappable step; cites none of the planar-cover literature and misdates the conjecture; part of a rapid series of same-creator 'wave point geometry' records; no uptake in four months, and later work (Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura, Jun 2026) still states the conjecture as open.
events.direction: confirmed

judgement.why: The conjecture is equivalent to K₁,₂,₂,₂ having no finite planar cover, so in-window work is partial. The Annor–Nikolayevsky–Payne fold<14 result dates to v1 (3 Nov 2023), before the snapshot; v2 restates the same result by fold number, so per F1 it stays pre-snapshot, and I scored it a bound (smallest possible counterexample fold). Negami's JMSJ theorem proves the 'only if' direction for the class of rotation-compatible covers: a case, digested by journal publication and by Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura's independent re-proof; its date is year-only 2024, so after_snapshot is null. The ANP 'Three theorems' paper rules out classes of planar covers of K₁,₂,₂,₂ (wheel-neighbourhood covers, certain face-length configurations, non-4-connected minimal covers), which I read as restricting the class of covers, hence case rather than none. Briański–Davies–Tan and Hliněný's Klein-bottle note are analogues on other surfaces (variant); the 2008 emulator construction concerns emulators, not covers (variant). The Matsuoka Zenodo claim is set aside as not_credible. No event involves any AI system.
judgement.doubts: Two close calls. (1) Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura re-proves a case already settled by Negami's 2024 paper; I scored it case because it does prove a restriction, but it adds no new case and could reasonably be scored none. (2) ANP 'Three theorems' could be read as mere structural constraints on a hypothetical counterexample (none) rather than settling a class of covers (case); the theorem wording in the record is partial. Negami 2024's earlier public version, if any, was not found; its content is secondhand via KST.
